div.div: طُلَّآءٌ , (Ibn-'Abbád, O, K,) like سُلَّآءٌ, (K, TA,) [in the CK, طَلّاء, like سَلّاء, and] in some copies of the K, erroneously, طِلَّآء, (TA,) Blood, itself: and some say, a pellicle upon the surface thereof: (O:) [and in like manner طُلَّآء is expl. in the K in art. طلأ:] or blood that has been made to go for nought, unretaliated, and uncompensated by a mulct: (K: [and from the context in the O, it seems that this is probably meant by Ibn- 'Abbád: see طُلٌّ:]) accord. to AAF, (TA,) the ء in this word is originally ل. (K, TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
